state.task: Audit the evidence quality of a FROZEN three-ticket research portfolio for Jamaica Lotto draw #2343 (6 main numbers from 1-38). Judge only the supplied evidence. This audit cannot change, reorder or replace any ticket, and its outputs are evidence judgments, not winning probabilities.

game_facts.note: Under a fair draw every fixed ticket has identical winning probability.

v1_science_ticket.selection: V1 seeded no-edge fallback (no V1 methodology passed the corrected evidence gate)

evidence_against: Exact ticket and candidate variants have not been backtested.
Frequency, gaps, pair lift and structure are descriptive, not independent predictive evidence.
Models share the same small dataset; agreement is correlated.
No qualifying independent out-of-sample support for this ticket.

v1_science_ticket.forensic_note: This exact ticket was also the V1 ticket for draws [2339, 2341]. The fixed-seed fallback with a <=2-overlap rule against the previous ticket mechanically alternates between the same candidate slots.

p0_protocol.status: frozen before the #2341 shadow; historical data through #2340 only

discovery_pool.basis: NO EDGE: predeclared default K=15 (no pool size passed on the development period)

p0_protocol.weight_formula: w_f = max(0, d_f) * h_f; d_f = dbar_f * n tau^2/(n tau^2 + 1); dbar_f = mean(x_f,u)/sigma; tau = 0.09; sigma = 0.112522; n >= 20
notes: E_pairs had no Holm-significant pair at any historical origin (flat).
Positive weights for B_recent and D_trend come from statistically null evidence after shrinkage (Holm p about 0.97).
Ticket score T = sum of weight x standardized component; portfolio objective J = T + incremental coverage of the pool, with pairwise overlap <= 2.

prospective_results_matches_by_track.note: live prospective draws only; one or few draws, descriptive only

forensic_2342.verdict: NO LOTTO V2/P1 REFINEMENT IS JUSTIFIED.

computed_sensitivity_research_only.description: Tickets 2-3 that the same algorithm would produce under alternative settings (NOT used; the frozen portfolio is unchanged).

t1_robustness.instructions: Consider ONLY ticket 1 at `portfolio[0]` in the context of the supplied evidence. How robust is the empirical evidence that this specific ticket is better than a random ticket?
criteria: No empirical support beyond random: every relevant methodology fails corrected testing and results match random controls.
Weak or fragile apparent support: small uncorrected differences, unstable across periods or settings.
Some repeatable out-of-sample support, but no corrected confirmation and substantial uncertainty.
Corrected confirmation-period support that is stable across sensitivity settings.
Strong support replicated across independent models, time periods and prospective outcomes.

t1_overfit.instructions: Consider ONLY ticket 1 at `portfolio[0]` in the context of the supplied evidence. Is chance or overfitting a better explanation of any apparent support for this ticket than a reproducible predictive signal?

criteria.true: Apparent support is compatible with noise: corrected tests fail, gains vanish against random comparators, or support comes from in-sample fitting.
criteria.false: Support survives corrected, out-of-sample tests and random-control comparisons.

t1_weak_evidence.instructions: Consider ONLY ticket 1 at `portfolio[0]` in the context of the supplied evidence. Does the selection of this ticket depend mainly on evidence that failed corrected statistical validation (or on a mechanical rule rather than evidence)?

criteria.true: Its selection rests on unvalidated weights, shrunk null evidence, coverage mechanics or a seeded fallback.
criteria.false: Its selection rests mainly on evidence that passed corrected validation.

t1_concentration.instructions: Consider ONLY ticket 1 at `portfolio[0]` in the context of the supplied evidence. Is whatever support this ticket has concentrated in one model family or in correlated families (for example B_recent and D_trend, which are correlated), rather than spread across genuinely independent evidence?

criteria.true: Support comes from one family or from families that share information.
criteria.false: Support comes from several genuinely independent families.

t1_fragility.instructions: Consider ONLY ticket 1 at `portfolio[0]` in the context of the supplied evidence. Would modest, reasonable changes to the construction (pool size, shrinkage strength, removing the weak evidence weights, tie-breaks) likely replace most of this ticket? Use `computed_sensitivity_research_only` where it applies.

criteria.true: Most of the ticket changes under reasonable alternative settings.
criteria.false: The ticket stays largely the same under reasonable alternative settings.

portfolio_robustness.instructions: Consider the WHOLE three-ticket portfolio at `portfolio` together with `portfolio_facts`, `p0_protocol` and `historical_confirmation_40_draws`. How robust is the evidence that this portfolio as a whole outperforms three diversified random tickets?
criteria: No empirical support beyond random: every relevant methodology fails corrected testing and results match random controls.
Weak or fragile apparent support: small uncorrected differences, unstable across periods or settings.
Some repeatable out-of-sample support, but no corrected confirmation and substantial uncertainty.
Corrected confirmation-period support that is stable across sensitivity settings.
Strong support replicated across independent models, time periods and prospective outcomes.

portfolio_edge.instructions: Consider the WHOLE three-ticket portfolio at `portfolio` together with `portfolio_facts`, `p0_protocol` and `historical_confirmation_40_draws`. Does the supplied evidence show that this portfolio has a higher expected number of matches than random diversified tickets?

criteria.true: A corrected historical test passed and the comparison with random portfolios excludes zero.
criteria.false: The historical gate failed or the comparison intervals include zero.

portfolio_overfit.instructions: Consider the WHOLE three-ticket portfolio at `portfolio` together with `portfolio_facts`, `p0_protocol` and `historical_confirmation_40_draws`. Is chance or overfitting a better explanation of any favourable historical or shadow result of this portfolio than a reproducible signal?

criteria.true: Favourable results are within random variation or depend on one draw.
criteria.false: Favourable results are corrected, repeatable and exceed random variation.

portfolio_concentration.instructions: Consider the WHOLE three-ticket portfolio at `portfolio` together with `portfolio_facts`, `p0_protocol` and `historical_confirmation_40_draws`. Is the evidence behind the challenger tickets concentrated in one model family or correlated families?

criteria.true: Challenger support comes mostly from one family or correlated families.
criteria.false: Challenger support is spread across independent families.

portfolio_coverage.instructions: Consider the WHOLE three-ticket portfolio at `portfolio` together with `portfolio_facts`, `p0_protocol` and `historical_confirmation_40_draws`. How well does the portfolio achieve its stated, non-predictive goal of covering many distinct model-supported numbers with low redundancy?
criteria: Poor: tickets largely duplicate each other and cover few distinct numbers.
Limited: substantial overlap; coverage little better than a single ticket plus noise.
Moderate: some overlap; coverage clearly broader than a single ticket.
Good: low overlap and broad coverage of the discovery pool.
Maximal: no overlap and the widest feasible coverage of the discovery pool.
